content.text: {"concept_key":"c3-maths-addition-3digit","title":"Adding 3-digit numbers with carrying","quick":"Add digits column by column starting from ones. If a column adds to 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry the ten to the next column.","full":"Think of buying items at a kirana shop: 345 rupees worth of rice plus 278 rupees worth of oil. Add ones first: 5+8=13, write 3 carry 1. Then tens: 4+7+1(carry)=12, write 2 carry 1. Then hundreds: 3+2+1(carry)=6. Answer: 623. The key: always add from the right (ones) side, and any carry moves exactly one column left, never skips.","traps":["Forgetting to carry the extra ten to the next column","Adding from left (hundreds) side instead of right","Writing both digits of a two-digit sum in one column instead of carrying"],"misconception":"Child thinks you can add any column first in any order without carrying forward properly, as if each column is independent.","parent_questions":[{"q":"Why do we start adding from the ones column and not the hundreds column?","expected_answer_hint":"Because carrying moves from right to left; starting left would miss carries needed for correct total."},{"q":"If ones column adds to 13, what do you write and what do you carry?","expected_answer_hint":"Write 3 in ones place, carry 1 to tens column."}],"check_question":{"q":"456 + 237 = ?","options":["693","683","793"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! You carried properly in each column.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite. Add ones first (6+7=13, carry 1), then tens (5+3+1=9), then hundreds (4+2=6) = 693."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A child and a shopkeeper at a small Indian kirana shop counting rupee coins and notes on a wooden counter.","labels":[{"text":"345","position":"left"},{"text":"278","position":"right"},{"text":"carry","position":"top"},{"text":"623","position":"bottom"}]}}
